entries.reasoning: TravelHub provides distribution and booking services to hotel operators in the GCC rather than operating hotels directly, placing it under the extended definition of a Hospitality Business under Section 1.11, and the services involve AI and data analytics relating to hotel properties in the UAE and KSA.
readings: TravelHub is caught as a Hospitality Business because it provides distribution services to hotel operators in the GCC under Section 1.11.
TravelHub is a consumer travel planning platform rather than a hotel owner or operator, placing it outside the core scope of a hospitality business.

incomingClauses.quote: Partner Hotel Ranking Module — a ranking and recommendation service that scores, ranks and surfaces Partner Hotels in the United Arab Emirates and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia to TravelHub users at the point of search and itinerary building, taking into account user fit, price competitiveness, partner commission tier, availability and conversion likelihood, and that drives the sort order of hotel results and "recommended stay" placements for booking through the TravelHub App;

entries.suggestedChange: Carve out Clause 4.1(b) (Partner Hotel Ranking Module) from the scope of work, or seek a written waiver from Al Noor Hospitality Group.
entries.waiverWhy: The Al Noor waiver is strictly limited to demand-forecasting services for Seaside Hotels LLC in Muscat, Oman, and explicitly excludes all other entities and GCC operations.
entries.impact: Arguably collides with the Al Noor non-compete commitment, which runs through September 2029.
